title_en:
I helped start OpenAI because I want AGI to be safe and beneficial for people. This post provides transparency that can be the foundation of industry-wide shared safety bars.

Perhaps the most important concept from the post is the following: "AI will also significantly contribute to progress on alignment and monitoring, I think that progress is unlikely to be fast enough to allow the full potential acceleration in pretraining."

Towards ensuring that safety keeps pace with general intelligence of pretrained models (as measured by "perplexity"), the post proposes "common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors)."

The general idea is to create a first shared limit, on some shared key metric, along with concrete exit criteria that would allow going beyond that. This can lead to a "common framework for setting successive limits and pacing further development".

Excited to move forward the conversation on pacing towards shared standards that are rooted in the science!

@john__allard Yes. The paper that popularized tool calls by LLMs, Toolformer, was published by my former colleagues at FAIR in January 2023.
But my slides makes a specific statement that is correct: ***auto-regressive*** LLMs have a basic flaw.
You can fix it by making them no auto-regressive, e.g. by backtracking, search, tool use, multiple trial and error, etc.
One of the main points of my talks, and the main point of this slide, has been to advocate for inference/reasoning by ***search***, as opposed to auto-regressive prediction.

title_en:
I just gave an AI trading agent its first trading assignment.

My instruction was simple: build a BTC trend-following strategy using the EMA crossover.

But what happened next was more interesting than I expected.

Using @FensoryApp , I went through the strategy-building process with its AI agent.

It asked me questions about:

- The asset and timeframe.
- Trade direction and leverage.
- Maximum position size.
- Stop-loss configuration.

I settled on BTC perpetuals, a 1-hour timeframe, 1x leverage, a maximum $10 position and a 2x ATR stop.

Then came the backtest.

Over the previous 90 days, the strategy generated 21 hypothetical positions. 

Only 2 were profitable, while 19 were losses.

The overall simulated result was -9.3%, with a maximum drawdown of 18.11%.

Not exactly the outcome I was hoping for.

But here's the interesting part.

Rather than simply presenting the result, the agent flagged the high stop-loss hit rate (76%) and suggested exploring a wider stop-loss with the same dollar risk.

It even offered to design a second version of the strategy.

No live trade was executed. 

This was a historical backtest, not a real trading result.

Not my first time trading but this is my first time actually putting a trading idea through an AI agent, and I can already see the possibilities.

Not because it magically knows how to make money, 

But because it can help translate an idea into rules, test those rules and identify areas that might need improvement.

I will be exploring Fensory a whole lot this week.

full_text_zh:
我刚刚给人工智能交易代理分配了第一个交易任务。

我的指示很简单：使用 EMA 交叉构建 BTC 趋势跟踪策略。

但接下来发生的事情比我想象的更有趣。

使用 @FensoryApp ，我通过其 AI 代理完成了策略构建过程。

它问了我以下问题：

- 资产和时间范围。
- 贸易方向和杠杆。
- 最大头寸规模。
- 止损配置。

我选择了 BTC 永续合约、1 小时时间框架、1 倍杠杆、最高 10 美元头寸和 2 倍 ATR 止损。

然后是回测。

在过去 90 天内，该策略生成了 21 个假设头寸。

其中只有2家盈利，19家亏损。

总体模拟结果为-9.3%，最大回撤为18.11%。

这不完全是我所希望的结果。

但这是有趣的部分。

该代理人并没有简单地展示结果，而是指出了较高的止损命中率（76%），并建议在相同的美元风险下探索更广泛的止损。

它甚至提出设计该战略的第二个版本。

没有执行任何实时交易。

这是历史回测，而不是真实的交易结果。

这不是我第一次交易，但这是我第一次真正通过人工智能代理提出交易想法，而且我已经看到了可能性。

不是因为它神奇地知道如何赚钱，

但因为它可以帮助将想法转化为规则，所以测试这些规则并确定可能需要改进的领域。

本周我将大量探索 Fensory。

title_en:
i wouldn't trust an AI agent with my entire portfolio just because it has a good-looking interface or promises to make smart decisions.

personally, i'd want to use it for a while before relying on it.

i'd pay attention to the small things first.

does it follow my instructions consistently? does it make its actions easy to understand? does the experience feel predictable, or am i constantly wondering what it's doing?

that's the kind of experience i want to see from @meetmotes.

i don't think people will start trusting AI agents simply because the technology becomes more advanced.

they'll trust them after using them repeatedly and seeing that they actually do what they're supposed to do.

for me, that's how an AI agent earns a place in someone's financial routine.

not through big promises, but through everyday reliability.

title_en:
WTF IS META DOING.

Meta's Muse AI agent has 10M+ downloads, is the #2 free app on the iPhone App Store, and it's reading end-to-end encrypted Signal messages and dropping bank balances into random chats.

Reuters dug up internal complaints from Meta's own staff. A Meta employee got a reminder from Muse to reply to her sister on Signal even though she never granted access, and the AI Now Institute independently reproduced it.

Another employee chatting about fishing weather got hit with: "BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57." They never shared bank info with Muse. Meta called those exact numbers "hallucinations."

Earlier the Mac app read a writer's messages after being told no, and this week The Hacker News showed a malicious webpage attack that hijacks Muse to steal private chats and memories.

Delete this spyware or run your agents locally where you can see what they touch.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: SpaceX首席执行官埃隆·马斯克指出，由于AI算力部署与营收产生之间存在数月的结算时滞，数据中心建设明年将产生数千亿美元的营运资金缺口。市场数据显示，SpaceX的信用违约互换（CDS）溢价已升至275个基点，远高于微软与谷歌等科技巨头，显示金融市场对其资本支出模式的风险评估趋于保守。
